sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Fifteen papers are selected from the latest biology/biomedicine announcement batch: seven new submissions, six newly surfaced category listings whose first submissions were earlier, and two substantive revisions. The clearest recurring pattern is computational methods being tested against molecular or assay data, with important gaps between in-silico performance and experimental or clinical validation. Spoken agenda: resistance enzymes, siRNA potency and perturbation response; protein mutation and conjugate design; sequencing adjudication; then biomedical modeling, imaging, and two revised studies. arXiv has no official trending chart; this relevance-ranked list is inferred from incomplete arXiv coverage and is not a measured popularity ranking. Semantic Scholar returned zero citations and zero influential citations for all 15 papers at the snapshot, so citation momentum does not support a popularity ranking. The entries below are therefore “Notable recent papers,” ranked by direct relevance and checkable research evidence, not by readership, downloads, or author reputation. Acceptance and journal comments are reported as publication-status signals only; limited secondary write-ups are not treated as popularity measures.
sections.subtitle: 15 papers

sections.title: Deep learning-guided discovery reveals the diversity and mutational potential of environmental beta-lactamases
sections.abstract: The authors combine protein-language-model representations and ensemble learning to identify environmental beta-lactamase candidates, then report resistance assays for two divergent enzymes and mutation effects.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report identifying more than 46,000 putative environmental beta-lactamases and finding that two divergent class-C candidates expressed in *E. coli* confer resistance to multiple beta-lactams; predicted substitutions altered resistance profiles.
sections.unique_caveat: The full paper states that experimental characterization covered only two class-C candidates and resistance was assessed primarily by MIC. It does not establish environmental prevalence, transmission, or human risk.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct antimicrobial-resistance and protein-function relevance; the authors report expression and antibiotic testing, including MIC measurements, rather than sequence prediction alone. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: The authors combine protein-language-model representations and ensemble learning to identify environmental beta-lactamase candidates, then report resistance assays for two divergent enzymes and mutation effects.
sections.subtitle: Biochemistry & proteins; DNA & genomics

sections.title: Silscore: modelling siRNA potency with positional thermodynamics and data-selected nucleotide-identity terms
sections.abstract: Silscore is a compact guide-sequence-only model combining overall and position-specific duplex thermodynamics with sparse nucleotide-identity terms to estimate siRNA potency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that the 26-parameter model has the highest observed Pearson correlation in three transfer evaluations; on Katoh–Suzuki, the data support an advantage over each applicable comparator. The paper also reports that some other comparisons are inconclusive.
sections.unique_caveat: These are retrospective dataset evaluations, not prospective silencing experiments. The guide-only model omits target-site accessibility and transcript context by design.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct RNA silencing-design question; tested on the Huesken split, Mixset, Katoh–Suzuki, and an unseen-target transfer setting. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: Silscore is a compact guide-sequence-only model combining overall and position-specific duplex thermodynamics with sparse nucleotide-identity terms to estimate siRNA potency.
sections.subtitle: RNA & transcriptomics; Biochemistry & proteins

sections.title: Predicting transcriptional interactions with GrnPFN
sections.abstract: GrnPFN uses simulated gene-regulatory-network screens for pretraining, then predicts non-additive transcriptional responses to combined perturbations from single-perturbation profiles and limited measured combinations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports better prediction than tested gradient-boosting and kernel-ridge baselines when combination measurements are absent or limited, with the relative advantage diminishing as screen-specific combinations accumulate.
sections.unique_caveat: The full paper notes that several later partitions reused cells, perturbation-pair folds overlap in members or compounds, and an additional drug–gene evaluation involved one drug in one cell line. Predicted transcriptional non-additivity does not itself establish a molecular mechanism or synergy in other phenotypes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct gene-regulation and single-cell perturbation focus; the paper evaluates CRISPR activation, RNA knockdown, and drug combinations and includes an additional CRISPRi–drug screen. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: GrnPFN uses simulated gene-regulatory-network screens for pretraining, then predicts non-additive transcriptional responses to combined perturbations from single-perturbation profiles and limited measured combinations.
sections.subtitle: RNA & transcriptomics; Gene regulation & epigenetics

sections.title: MutAtlas: A PDB-Wide Energy-Guided Atlas of Protein Mutation Effects
sections.abstract: MutAtlas assembles mutation signals from physics-based, protein-language, and inverse-folding models across experimentally resolved structures, then proposes disagreement-aware distillation for zero-shot mutation-effect prediction.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that their method, trained without experimental mutation labels, had the best overall performance among evaluated zero-shot baselines and naive fusion strategies on ProteinGym; the full-text table reports 0.498 overall macro-averaged Spearman correlation.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a computational benchmark result using model-generated training signals, not experimental or clinical validation. Generalization across proteins, assays, and engineering decisions remains to be tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein mutation interpretation and engineering relevance; cross-listed in genomics; the arXiv comment says accepted at ICML 2026. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: MutAtlas assembles mutation signals from physics-based, protein-language, and inverse-folding models across experimentally resolved structures, then proposes disagreement-aware distillation for zero-shot mutation-effect prediction.
sections.subtitle: Biochemistry & proteins; Bioinformatics & sequence analysis

sections.title: CupOFMoCA: Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly
sections.abstract: CupOFMoCA generates PROTACs and peptide–drug conjugates while enforcing cross-component chemical constraints during generation rather than filtering invalid assemblies afterward.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved valid-conjugate yield over matched post-hoc filtering for peptide–drug conjugates and the highest assembly validity on two of three PROTAC systems; they also report post-hoc scoring and molecular-dynamics analyses.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is computational generation, predicted scoring, and simulation; the paper does not establish experimentally measured degradation, binding, or therapeutic efficacy for generated molecules.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct molecular-conjugate design application; arXiv comment identifies publication at NeurIPS 2026. The abstract reports evaluations across three peptide–drug-conjugate and three PROTAC systems. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: CupOFMoCA generates PROTACs and peptide–drug conjugates while enforcing cross-component chemical constraints during generation rather than filtering invalid assemblies afterward.
sections.subtitle: Biochemistry & proteins; Biomedical & translational medicine

sections.title: AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication for Automated, Auditable Read-Level Review in Cancer Diagnostic Sequencing
sections.abstract: AVA uses auditable agent workflows to inspect read-level sequencing evidence for borderline low-variant-allele-frequency calls, evaluated on a DNA-sequencing benchmark and patient RNA-seq data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that tested closed- and open-weight agents outperformed the best VAF/depth thresholds on a subsample of borderline variants, returning auditable reasoning traces.
sections.unique_caveat: Benchmark results do not establish performance in routine prospective laboratories, diagnostic error reduction, turnaround-time improvement, or patient benefit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct cancer-sequencing workflow relevance; the abstract names the SEQC2 DNA-seq benchmark and patient RNA-seq data, and the arXiv comment reports acceptance to the ML4H 2026 Findings Track. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: AVA uses auditable agent workflows to inspect read-level sequencing evidence for borderline low-variant-allele-frequency calls, evaluated on a DNA-sequencing benchmark and patient RNA-seq data.

sections.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
sections.abstract: An amino-acid alphabet permutation that preserves alignment statistics disrupts contact predictions from tested protein language models, unlike the classical Potts and inverse-covariance estimators.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across nine proteins, the authors report that global residue relabeling sharply reduces model contact-map overlap while Potts predictions remain invariant, which they interpret as evidence of “alphabet anchoring.”
sections.unique_caveat: The full paper limits the evaluation to a relatively small set of short, mostly single-domain proteins and three model families. The authors state that invariance is necessary but not sufficient evidence for pure coevolutionary inference; retrained or fine-tuned models were not tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein-model interpretability result; tests ESM-2, MSA Transformer, and AMPLIFY across multiple scales; the arXiv comment reports acceptance to the ICBINB failure-modes workshop at NeurIPS 2026. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: An amino-acid alphabet permutation that preserves alignment statistics disrupts contact predictions from tested protein language models, unlike the classical Potts and inverse-covariance estimators.

sections.title: Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model
sections.abstract: The authors model target–ligand binding as sums of interaction “pixels” and use affinity distributions from a naive DNA-encoded library to estimate the complexity and expected yield of a focused follow-up library.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say the model translates a desired number of tight binders into an estimated library size and supplies a random-design baseline against which machine-learning or active-learning designs could be assessed.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model-based sizing method inferred from existing affinity distributions; no prospective synthesis-and-selection test of the predicted second-generation library is reported.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomolecular binding and medicinal-chemistry data-design relevance; cross-listed in biomolecules. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: The authors model target–ligand binding as sums of interaction “pixels” and use affinity distributions from a naive DNA-encoded library to estimate the complexity and expected yield of a focused follow-up library.

sections.title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
sections.abstract: This review frames a biological model’s “knowledge boundary” around data, architecture, training, evaluation, and post-analysis, to make reliability limits explicit for researchers and tool-using agents.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors synthesize evidence about where biological foundation models succeed or fail and propose standardized descriptions of the conditions under which their outputs are reliable.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a review and framework proposal, not a new comparative benchmark or prospective demonstration that the framework improves biological decisions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad biological foundation-model scope; the arXiv comment says it is to be published in Annual Review of Biomedical Data Science. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: This review frames a biological model’s “knowledge boundary” around data, architecture, training, evaluation, and post-analysis, to make reliability limits explicit for researchers and tool-using agents.

sections.title: Stage-Resolved EBV-Induced B-Cell Programs Across CNS Selection and Multiple Sclerosis Compartments
sections.abstract: A cross-dataset reanalysis reports compartment- and stage-dependent EBV-associated B-cell transcriptional programs, rather than a stable signature shared across blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that a frozen EBV-associated B-cell factor did not predict MS activity (AUC 0.487; p=0.489), and that early and late EBV-associated transcriptional programs showed opposing directions across compartments.
sections.unique_caveat: This is retrospective reanalysis with small samples for key contrasts, including nine evaluable human CSF participants and five EBV-exposed mice. The authors state that no external program met their prespecified prospective criterion; the results do not establish causation or a validated biomarker.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper appeared in the 13 November q-bio.GN recent-list batch as a category listing; its arXiv record retains the earlier first-submission date shown above. The abstract reports human and humanized-mouse data with anatomical, sequencing-depth, and other controls. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: A cross-dataset reanalysis reports compartment- and stage-dependent EBV-associated B-cell transcriptional programs, rather than a stable signature shared across blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain.

sections.title: Stretched bilayer-cytoskeleton links hold echinocytes in a model splenic slit
sections.abstract: In a two-component red-cell model, stage III echinocytes required 37–50 times the pressure drop that passed an equal-area, equal-volume discocyte through a model splenic slit; stretched bilayer–cytoskeleton links were implicated in retention.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' model suggests spicule shape together with membrane loss can hinder passage through a splenic slit; lengthening the modeled links by about twofold released a held cell.
sections.unique_caveat: Central passage and link-stretch results are from simulated cells in a model slit, not a direct test of clearance in human spleens or transfusion outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct cell-mechanics and splenic-clearance question; cross-listed in cell biology and supported by a detailed mechanical study. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: In a two-component red-cell model, stage III echinocytes required 37–50 times the pressure drop that passed an equal-area, equal-volume discocyte through a model splenic slit; stretched bilayer–cytoskeleton links were implicated in retention.

sections.title: A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
sections.abstract: The authors propose an online method for choosing an individualized blood-pressure target and norepinephrine dose from a short MAP/dose record, using a reduced PK/PD model and uncertainty propagation to limit predicted hypotension risk.
sections.claimed_contribution: In the virtual cohort, the method recommended a dose for 74% at a nominal 5% risk; 6.9% of patients receiving recommendations had a MAP reading below 65 mmHg, compared with 25% under a fixed 70 mmHg target applied to the full virtual cohort.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is not a prospective clinical trial: recommendations were assessed retrospectively under doses actually administered and in virtual patients. It does not establish clinical benefit or safety.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct perioperative biomedical decision-modeling question; the abstract reports retrospective-record calibration and a cohort of 4,096 virtual patients. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: The authors propose an online method for choosing an individualized blood-pressure target and norepinephrine dose from a short MAP/dose record, using a reduced PK/PD model and uncertainty propagation to limit predicted hypotension risk.

sections.title: A Feasibility Study of Whole-Cerebrum Task-Based fMRI at 0.55 T: Motor and Visual Tasks Using Single-Shot EPI
sections.abstract: In six healthy participants, the authors detected motor- and visual-task activation at 0.55 T and report that concatenating two five-minute runs increased activation statistics and reduced voxelwise background dispersion.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that whole-cerebrum task fMRI was feasible with single-shot EPI at 0.55 T; a representative 3 T dataset is used for reference, and the abstract reports that longer low-field acquisition could approach 3 T statistical significance over the compared durations.
sections.unique_caveat: Only six healthy participants were studied; the 3 T reference is not described as a matched-cohort comparison, and this does not establish clinical diagnostic performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct medical-physics imaging feasibility question with a stated healthy-participant sample and task comparison. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: In six healthy participants, the authors detected motor- and visual-task activation at 0.55 T and report that concatenating two five-minute runs increased activation statistics and reduced voxelwise background dispersion.

sections.title: TRACED-X enables in vivo imaging of cellular microstructure, intrinsic extracellular diffusivity, tortuosity, and membrane permeability in human glioma patients
sections.abstract: TRACED-X uses Monte Carlo-generated diffusion signals and neural-network estimators to infer tumor microstructure and transport parameters, with a proof-of-concept application to eight glioma patients.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report simultaneous in-vivo estimates of cellular and extracellular parameters, with maps coherent with radiological findings and expected tumor phenotypes.
sections.unique_caveat: Eight patients support feasibility only; the authors say broader patient studies are needed to assess clinical utility. This is not a validated diagnostic or treatment tool.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Substantive v2 update says it adds experiments in response to reviewer suggestions; under review at Magnetic Resonance in Medicine. The abstract reports eight mixed-grade glioma patients. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: TRACED-X uses Monte Carlo-generated diffusion signals and neural-network estimators to infer tumor microstructure and transport parameters, with a proof-of-concept application to eight glioma patients.

sections.title: Symmetry-Induced Conservation Laws, Three-Channel Attribution, and Solid-Phase Recycling in Prebiotic Enantiomeric Excess Amplification
sections.abstract: The revised paper derives conservation and attribution identities for mirror-symmetric reaction networks and re-analyzes experimental benchmark systems for chiral amplification and phase partitioning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that apparent enantiomeric-excess gains can reflect phase partitioning and mass loss rather than new parity-breaking synthesis, and report model-derived yields for coupled recycling schemes.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a theoretical framework and re-analysis of existing systems, not new experimental confirmation of the proposed yield mechanisms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct prebiotic-chemistry relevance and a v2 update in the batch; the abstract reports analyses of seven experimental benchmark systems. Semantic Scholar snapshot: 0 citations, 0 influential citations.
sections.content: The revised paper derives conservation and attribution identities for mirror-symmetric reaction networks and re-analyzes experimental benchmark systems for chiral amplification and phase partitioning.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: - **Modeling molecular function needs context-specific validation.** The beta-lactamase study includes limited expression/MIC testing; Silscore evaluates retrospective potency datasets; GrnPFN predicts non-additive transcription; MutAtlas and the invariant-relabeling study test protein-model signals; and CupOFMoCA and the DEL paper assess generated or planned binding designs computationally. Their targets and evidence types differ, so the set supports an evaluation theme, not a single validated AI capability. - **RNA and perturbation models emphasize transfer.** Silscore tests potency transfer across datasets/targets, while GrnPFN evaluates combination-response predictions across perturbation screens. Both remain bounded by the particular data splits, target contexts, and readouts used. - **Translation claims remain bounded by study design.** AVA is evaluated on sequencing datasets; the EBV report is a reanalysis with small human and mouse contrasts; and the red-cell, perioperative, and low-field fMRI papers each have different model, cohort, or feasibility limits. These papers do not collectively establish clinical benefit or a field-wide clinical shift. - **New revisions in this batch:** TRACED-X adds experiments after review and still reports only eight glioma patients; the prebiotic-chirality update adds analysis of existing benchmark systems, not new experiments. Both are revisions, not new papers.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: These follow-ups are grounded in the limitations reported by the selected authors and are research proposals, not clinical advice. - **Expand enzyme-function validation.** The beta-lactamase authors identify two class-C candidates as experimentally characterized and call for broader functional testing. A next study could sample divergent candidates from all Ambler classes, pair MICs with direct hydrolysis, expression, and stability assays, then test predicted substitutions across sequence backgrounds and controlled antibiotic exposures. - **Freeze and prospectively test transfer models.** For Silscore, preregister a guide-only prediction set across targets and laboratories, then compare with models incorporating target accessibility and transcript context. For GrnPFN, prospectively measure unseen perturbation pairs in independent cell lines and screens, separating cells used for inputs from those used for evaluation and checking whether predicted transcriptional non-additivity corresponds to other phenotypes. - **Compare model-derived protein signals with new experiments.** Test MutAtlas predictions on proteins and assays outside ProteinGym using focused deep-mutational scanning; stratify calibration and ranking by cross-model disagreement. For CupOFMoCA and the DEL sizing method, synthesize selected generated or focused-library compounds and measure binding, assembly validity, and functional effects against predefined baselines. - **Validate diagnostic and clinical models prospectively.** AVA needs blinded multi-laboratory assessment with adjudicated variants and prespecified false-positive/false-negative and turnaround measures. The perioperative blood-pressure method needs prospective evaluation with predefined clinician override and safety endpoints. The 0.55 T fMRI result needs a larger same-subject 0.55/3 T study with repeat scans and patient cohorts before clinical-performance claims. - **Test EBV compartment hypotheses longitudinally.** The EBV reanalysis itself calls for virologic, clonotypic, antigen-specific, epigenetic, and longitudinal evidence. A follow-up could measure paired blood/CSF samples over time with prespecified external validation, rather than inferring ancestry from transcriptional resemblance alone. - **Validate the two revised studies beyond their current evidence.** TRACED-X needs larger independent glioma cohorts with test-retest and pathology comparisons; the prebiotic-chirality paper motivates closed- and open-system experiments that separately track soluble and solid chiral mass, racemization, and product formation.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This 15-paper batch is most notable for methods that expose the limits of model transfer or reveal how much validation is still needed. A few papers report experimental or patient-derived data, but the strongest claims remain bounded by small experimental panels, retrospective datasets, or computational evaluation. The ranking reflects relevance, not measured arXiv popularity, and arXiv alone is incomplete biomedical coverage.
